correctness.rationale: For each finite block the eigenvalues are \(e^{i\theta_j}\) in the nonorthogonal basis used by the construction. Monotonicity of the positive phases gives finite total variation of \(e^{-i\theta_j}\), so the same partial-sum-projection summation-by-parts estimate bounds the inverse blocks uniformly. For rotated Cesàro kernels \(F_m(t)=m^{-1}\sum_{k=1}^m e^{ikt}\), the identity \(F_m(-t)=\overline{F_m(t)}\) makes the variation sequence for \(\phi-\theta_j\) exactly the forward variation sequence at rotation \(-\phi\). Thus the block-uniform forward multiplier estimate transfers unchanged to \(T^{-1}\). The original signed-average obstruction remains a forward property of the same \(T\), so failure of strong Cesàro boundedness persists.
